test_title: PYST 10: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 12 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which state government introduced the Drone Promotion and Utilisation Policy, 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madhya Pradesh** became the first Indian state to introduce the **Drone Promotion and Utilisation Policy, 2025.**
 
• The policy aims to promote the use of **drones** in various sectors, including agriculture, industrial inspections, surveillance, disaster management, and healthcare delivery.
 
• It includes provisions to create a **drone ecosystem** in the state, which will foster innovation, research, and entrepreneurship. *Hence, this initiative is a significant step towards technological advancement in Madhya Pradesh.*
 
• The policy also focuses on **training and skill development** to create a workforce capable of handling drone operations and maintenance. It encourages collaboration between academic institutions and industries to build drone technology expertise.
 
• Madhya Pradesh’s initiative aligns with the **Digital India campaign**, contributing to the country’s vision of becoming a global hub for drone technology. *Hence, the correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Drone Technology and its Applications:**

 
 
• **Drones** are unmanned aerial vehicles used for various applications, including **remote sensing, aerial photography, and delivery services.**
 
• In agriculture, drones can be used for **crop monitoring, pesticide spraying, and soil analysis**, improving productivity and efficiency.
 
• Drones are also critical in **disaster management**, helping with **rescue operations, damage assessment, and relief distribution** in affected areas.
 
 
 
• **Government Regulations on Drones:**
 
 
• The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) introduced the **Drone Rules, 2021**, which simplify the process for owning and operating drones in India.
 
• The rules include provisions for **online registration, reduced fees, and the creation of a Digital Sky platform** to manage drone operations.
 
• The government aims to make India a **global drone hub** by **2030.**
 
 
 
• **Other States and Drone Initiatives:**
 
 
• States like **Jharkhand**, **Punjab**, and **Odisha** are also exploring opportunities to integrate drones into their governance and development plans.
 
• These states focus on adopting drones for **agriculture, healthcare, and infrastructure development.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Drone Promotion and Utilisation Policy Highlights:**

 
 
• The policy includes measures to **attract private investments** in the drone industry, aiming to create a robust infrastructure for research and development.
 
• It emphasizes collaboration with industries to establish **testing and certification facilities** for drones, ensuring compliance with national and international standards.
 
 
 
• **Global Drone Market:**
 
 
• **India** is emerging as a key player in the **global drone market**, which is expected to grow significantly by **2025.**
 
• The adoption of drone technology is accelerating across sectors such as **defense, logistics, and healthcare**, contributing to economic growth.
